mushrooms.title: Five mushrooms. Five stories.
mushrooms.subtitle: Each mushroom carries centuries of traditional use. Science is only beginning to understand why.

cordyceps.name: Cordyceps
cordyceps.description: Growing above 4,000m on the Tibetan plateau, Cordyceps has one of nature's most remarkable life cycles — it parasitizes insects, then fruits from their bodies. Tibetan nomads and practitioners have incorporated it into their food traditions for 800+ years. Over 200 published studies now examine its unique compounds including cordycepin and adenosine.

lions_mane.name: Lion's Mane
lions_mane.description: Cascading white tendrils give Lion's Mane its unmistakable appearance. Known as the 'mountain priest mushroom' in Japan, it has been used in Buddhist monastery food traditions across China, Korea and Japan for centuries. It contains hericenones and erinacines — compounds found nowhere else in nature — which are the subject of ongoing scientific interest.

reishi.name: Reishi
reishi.description: Called 'Lingzhi' (靈芝) in Chinese — meaning 'spirit plant' — Reishi has been documented in Chinese food and wellness culture for over 4,000 years. Reserved for royalty and recorded in the Ming Dynasty pharmacopeia Bencao Gangmu, its lacquered red surface has symbolized longevity across East Asian art and architecture for millennia.

chaga.name: Chaga
chaga.description: Growing for decades on birch trees in Siberia's -40°C forests, Chaga records among the highest ORAC (antioxidant) values of any food source. Brewed as tea for centuries in Russian and Scandinavian traditions, this mushroom develops extraordinary resilience adapting to extreme cold. It even appears in Solzhenitsyn's novel 'Cancer Ward' as a cultural touchstone.

turkey_tail.name: Turkey Tail
turkey_tail.description: Called 'Yun Zhi' (雲芝, cloud mushroom) in Chinese tradition, Turkey Tail grows on fallen logs in forests worldwide — nature's most democratic mushroom. Its vivid rainbow bands have symbolized natural beauty for centuries. It is currently the most scientifically studied functional mushroom in the world, with unique polysaccharides PSK and PSP drawing significant research attention.

about.title:
What nature took
millennia to perfect
about.description1: Long before modern science had the tools to examine them, people across the world had already discovered these mushrooms. Tibetan nomads, Siberian hunters, East Asian practitioners — centuries of lived experience pointed to the same five species. MYCO BLEND captures what they found, using modern extraction to do it with precision.
about.description2: We use only fruiting bodies — the actual mushroom, not the mycelium or substrate filler. The fruiting body is what traditional cultures used, and where active compounds like β-glucans are concentrated. Every batch is independently third-party tested for potency and safety, with results published.

process.title: Four steps. No shortcuts.
process.subtitle: From source to seal, every step is held to the highest standard.

harvest.title: Harvest
harvest.description: Fruiting bodies are harvested at peak β-glucan content. No mycelium, no substrate filler, no grain. Every ingredient is traceable to its origin farm or forest.

extract.title: Dual Extraction
extract.description: We use both hot water extraction (for water-soluble β-glucans) and alcohol extraction (for fat-soluble triterpenes). Inspired by traditional tea brewing methods — adapted for precision.

verify.title: Third-Party Testing
verify.description: Every batch is tested by an independent certified lab: β-glucan content, heavy metals, mycotoxins, microbial safety. Any batch that misses the mark is rejected entirely.

blend.title: Precision Blending
blend.description: Five extracts are combined in precise ratios in a GMP-certified facility. Nitrogen-flushed packaging protects freshness from seal to scoop.
